attributes.probed_form: A) BRANCH PAIR, four spellings of the inner test at src/game/ui/select.c:2715 inside `case 4:`. A1 empty-then: `if ((*(u16*)(pl + offsetof(Player, name) + offsetof(P_SAVE_HEAD, class_unlock)) & (known << (spec - 8))) != 0) { } else { known = 0; }` -> object bytes UNCHANGED, MWCC folds the empty arm and re-inverts (strong negative). A2 both-arms: same test with `{ known = 1; } else { known = 0; }` -> branch pair APPEARS (target-only becomes `(none)`), but costs a redundant `li`, 218/217. A3 both-arms with the literal shift `(1 << (spec - 8))` instead of `(known << (spec - 8))` -> byte-identical to A2, so MWCC already CSEs the two spellings of the constant. A4 ONE-CASE SWITCH: `known = 1; switch (*(u16*)(pl + offsetof(Player, name) + offsetof(P_SAVE_HEAD, class_unlock)) & (known << (spec - 8))) { case 0: known = 0; break; }` -> this is the form that WORKS: it emits the target's `beq`/`b` pair AND lets `known` share the register that already holds the shift constant, so no redundant `li`. B) SDATA SIZE: `extern char lbl_80347F4C[12];` at select.c:101 is WRONG -- config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt gives `lbl_80347F4C = .sdata2:0x80347F4C; // type:object size:0x8`. Correcting it to `[8]` puts the object under MWCC's 8-byte small-data threshold and produces the target's single `li r7,0 @lbl_80347F4C(EMB_SDA21)` in place of our `lis`+`addi`.
attributes.residual: The two clusters are ONE lever and the lever is blocked by a TU-WIDE POOL CASCADE, which is the finding. Correcting lbl_80347F4C's declared size is a genuine source-correctness fix and it is exactly what update_class_spec wants -- but the declaration is file-scope, and shrinking that one extern under the small-data threshold removes one entry from the TU's address-constant pool. do_player_select spills a run of address constants to its frame at +0x1a0..+0x1f4 (`lis`/`addi` pairs feeding `stw r0,NN(r1)` for lbl_80240E30, lbl_80120104, lbl_80121F88, lbl_80274578, gPlayers, lbl_80121FB0); with one fewer pooled constant that whole run reshapes and do_player_select loses 3 instructions the target has, costing +101 real. Net across the TU the pair is a LOSS, so it was not retained. WHAT IS PROVEN AND REUSABLE: (1) the one-case-switch form A4 is the source lever for a target-only `beq`+`b` branch pair, and it also unifies the flag variable with the shift constant; (2) the correct declared size of lbl_80347F4C is 8, not 12, and our tree is wrong about it. NEXT LANE, in order: verify against the retail do_player_select whether ITS lbl_80347F4C reference is genuinely the non-SDA form (the target rows I read at +0x1a0..+0x1f4 are OTHER symbols, so this was never confirmed); if retail really uses SDA at both sites, then our +101 at do_player_select is itself a repairable pool-order defect and fixing it unblocks update_class_spec's real 24 -> 8 in the same edit.
